question: P-1 and O-1 dynamic baseline audits (PRODUCT_AGNOSTIC ordered-plan step 8): hold one side of the stack fixed at a deterministic baseline and vary only the other side across the dynamic candidates and baselines, swept over the step-8 target axes (same-shape relabel, same-shape numeric perturbations, larger product count, larger producer count). Does the matrix keep contract failures distinct from policy failures, and how do entity_planner / learned-gate portable / planner-gated portable producers compare under a fixed `proportional` orderer, and proportional / even_split / obs_price / portable orderers compare under a fixed `stock_aware` producer?
plan: PRODUCT_AGNOSTIC.md ordered action plan step 8. No new policy code: reuses the EXP-0012 (orderer) + EXP-0013 (producer) checkpoints unchanged and the `transfer_matrix` runner. Adds two reusable same-shape target generators (`numeric_perturbation_targets` reusing `eval.generalization`; `producer_permutation_targets` reusing `permute_scale_config`), two named audit stack sets (`PRODUCER_AUDIT_STACKS`, `ORDERER_AUDIT_STACKS`), and a `transfer_matrix --audit {producer,orderer}` CLI mode. TDD'd in `tests/test_transfer_matrix.py`.

method.producer_audit: Hold orderer = proportional; vary producer over {noop (floor), entity_planner (bar), stock_aware, portable_scorer (learned gates), portable_scorer_planner_gates}. Stacks = PRODUCER_AUDIT_STACKS.
method.orderer_audit: Hold producer = stock_aware; vary orderer over {even_split, proportional, obs_price, portable_scorer}. Plus a noop+proportional floor row. Stacks = ORDERER_AUDIT_STACKS.
method.targets: Step-8 sweep off held-out depth-3 seeds 6-9: per-seed scale target + one same-shape capacity relabel (default_targets); same-shape numeric perturbations off s6 (degr2x, unseen quantity, lean0.7 capacity, cost1.5x); larger product (prodW8=24 products), larger producer (agentW8=24 producers), larger both (size_transfer_targets off s6). The orderer audit adds one producer-row permutation off s6 (equivariance). All numeric/relabel/permutation targets are dims-preserving by construction.

metric: Per cell: contract flags + runs_episode + failure_class + dead_rate; consumer_completed_units; ratio_vs_practical_baseline (vs entity_planner+proportional on the SAME target). The audit reads the value SPREAD across the varied side per target (the fixed side is constant), so a spread is a policy signal and a non-run is a contract signal.
pass: Audit deliverable, not a single accept/reject gate: (1) zero contract failures on every dynamic/portable cell across the step-8 target sweep (contract vs policy stays separable); (2) the floor (noop) stays 0 units (targets nontrivial); (3) the producer and orderer value spreads are reported per target so the next fix target is legible. Records which axes the portable modules win/tie/lose on under a fixed deterministic counterpart.
notes: Local eval only (HARD RULE: evaluation of existing checkpoints, no training). Out-of-family recipe targets are intentionally NOT in this step-8 sweep (covered separately by EXP-0017/0018 and deferred to steps 9-10). Shape-compatible legacy flat producers/orderers are unwired (no checkpoint) and contract-incompatible off-size, so they are recorded as omitted, not run.
